description: I am a class 9 student from India passionate about aerospace engineering and Python programming. For this solo entry, I am building an interactive Python space mission simulator using real NASA planetary physics data.
summary:
Mission Architect is an interactive, browser-based spacecraft systems-engineering and orbital mechanics simulator built around NASA's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) and Four Mission Segments (Launch, Space, Ground, and User). We developed a zero-latency web platform featuring four mission scenarios—a Low Earth Orbit Wildfire CubeSat (550 km), a Lunar South Pole Ice Lander (Shackleton Crater), a Mars Science Orbiter (300 km), and an unrestricted Deep-Space Sandbox.
Users configure launch vehicles, scientific instruments, solar or nuclear power systems, communications dishes, propellant mass, and retro-burn altitude while a live SVG spacecraft blueprint updates in real time with mass, cost, power margin, delta-v, and downlink badges. Upon ignition, an animated HTML5 Canvas engine simulates orbital insertion or powered lunar descent under dynamic space weather anomalies, followed by interactive GMAT-style telemetry graphs, a Commander Medal Leaderboard, and a single-attempt NASA Academy Quiz. This matters because it bridges the gap between isolated rocket equations and real-world NASA mission trade-offs for students and aspiring engineers worldwide.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Mission Architect is an interactive, browser-based spacecraft systems-engineering and orbital mechanics simulator structured around NASA's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) and Four Mission Segments (Launch, Space, Ground, and User). Users select from four mission modes—Low Earth Orbit Wildfire CubeSat (550 km), Lunar South Pole Ice Lander (Shackleton Crater), Mars Science Orbiter (300 km), or an unrestricted Deep-Space Sandbox—and configure launch vehicles, scientific payloads, solar or nuclear RTG power systems, deep-space communications dishes, propellant mass, and terminal retro-burn altitude. As players adjust parameters, a live SVG spacecraft blueprint dynamically reconfigures hardware components while updating real-time pre-launch constraint badges (Launch Mass, Mission Cost, Power Margin, Total Δv, Design Lifetime, and Ground Downlink %). Upon ignition, an HTML5 Canvas physics engine simulates orbital insertion or powered retro-descent under stochastic space weather anomalies (Coronal Mass Ejection solar flares, dust attenuation, and micrometeoroid impulses), followed by a 4-Segment Engineering Audit, real NASA Twin Mission comparisons, four interactive hover-enabled telemetry graphs, a Commander Medal Leaderboard, and a single-attempt NASA Academy Quiz.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Students and aspiring space engineers often learn Tsiolkovsky's Rocket Equation and orbital mechanics in isolation without seeing how real-world constraints collide. Mission Architect turns complex aerospace systems engineering into an intuitive, zero-barrier learning lab—helping learners worldwide grasp why heavier instruments reduce Δv, why deep-space missions require nuclear power or high-gain antennas, and how engineering safety margins protect spacecraft against solar storms.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:
• Frontend & Physics Simulation: HTML5 Canvas (animated ascent/descent kinematics and interactive telemetry charts), Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) for dynamic hardware stack blueprints, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
• Prototyping & Cloud Hosting: Python (initial physics validation in Google Colab), GitHub (version-controlled source repository), and Hugging Face Spaces (24/7 static cloud deployment at https://spark1608-mission-architect-nasa.static.hf.space).
• AI & Documentation Tools: Generative AI (assistive code structuring and UI refinement) and Google Workspace for technical documentation.

Creativity & Engineering Factors Considered:
Rather than relying on static calculators, we combined a real-time dynamic SVG rocket assembler, coupled multi-segment physics, real NASA twin-mission benchmarking (Landsat 9, LRO/VIPER, MRO/MAVEN, Psyche), and a strict single-attempt anti-guessing quiz that diagnoses misconceptions and unlocks +$10M innovation grants per correct answer. Key engineering factors modeled include Tsiolkovsky propellant mass ratios, specific impulse (Isp), lunar soft-touchdown velocity limits (≤ 3.5 m/s), +30 W solar-flare power survival margins, and ground-station downlink bandwidth bottlenecks.
